```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Purohit_2026_linezolid"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Purohit_2026_linezolid"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/ofid/ofag154> (open access, PMC13064523)

Purohit et al. describe linezolid pharmacokinetics in plasma and lumbar
cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from the ALTER trial, which randomised Ugandan adults
with tuberculous meningitis (TBM) to standard-dose (10 mg/kg) or high-dose
(35 mg/kg) rifampicin with or without linezolid for the first 4 weeks. The
final model is a one-compartment model with first-order absorption and linear
clearance, linked to a CSF effect compartment parameterised by a transfer rate
constant (`kp`) and a CSF-to-plasma partition coefficient (`PC`). The only
retained covariate is the absolute daily rifampicin dose: participants on 1650
or 2100 mg/day had a 34.2% higher linezolid clearance than those on 300, 450,
600 or 1200 mg/day.

# Population

Eighteen participants contributed 73 plasma and 30 CSF linezolid
concentrations (Results; Supplementary Table 2). Median age was 38.5 years
(range 26-72) and median weight 50 kg (range 34-69); 50% were female, and all
were living with HIV (6 on antiretroviral therapy). TBM was definite in 5,
probable in 12 and possible in 1 participant; MRC grade I/II/III in 27.8% /
50% / 22.2% (Table 1). Twelve participants received linezolid 1200 mg once
daily and 6 (inadvertently) 600 mg twice daily; 8 received high-dose and 10
standard-dose rifampicin. Plasma was sampled intensively on day 1 (0, 2, 4 and
8 h) and sparsely on day 14; one lumbar puncture per visit was randomised to
an early (0-2 h), medium (2-6 h) or late (6-8 h) window.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Purohit_2026_linezolid")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing at its source; the
table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` | log(0.40) 1/h | Table 2, ka 0.40 (0.19-0.61) |
| `lcl` | log(6.01) L/h | Table 2, CL 6.01 (5.01-7.01) |
| `lvc` | log(27.70) L | Table 2, V 27.70 (16.27-38.77) |
| `lfdepot` | fixed(log(1)) | Table 2, F relative bioavailability 1 (fixed) |
| `lke0` (paper `kp`) | log(0.383) 1/h | Table 2, kp 0.383 (0.282-0.484) |
| `lppc` (paper `PC`) | log(0.535) | Table 2, PC 0.535 (0.458-0.612) |
| `e_dose_rifampicin_cl` | 0.342 | Table 2, effect of 1650 or 2100 mg rifampicin on CL 34.2% (2.4-66.4) |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.177^2) | Table 2, IIV on CL 17.7% CV |
| `etalke0` | log(1 + 0.925^2) | Table 2, IIV on kp 92.5% CV |
| `propSd` | 0.333 | Table 2, plasma proportional error 33.3% |
| `addSd` | 0.26 mg/L | Table 2, plasma additive error 0.26 ug/mL |
| `propSd_Ccsf` | 0.316 | Table 2, CSF proportional error 31.6% |
| One-compartment, first-order absorption, linear CL | n/a | Results, Pharmacokinetic Model; Figure 1 |
| `d/dt(csf) <- ke0 * (ppc * Cc - csf)` | n/a | Figure 1 and caption (kp rate, PC extent); Discussion ("hypothetical effect compartment") |
| `cl` x (1 + 0.342) when rifampicin >= 1650 mg/day | n/a | Results paragraph after Figure 1; Table 2 |
| Plasma combined, CSF proportional residual error | n/a | Results, Pharmacokinetic Model |

# Virtual cohort

The individual data are not public. The cohort below reproduces the paper's
simulation design (Methods, Simulations): linezolid 1200 mg once daily or
600 mg twice daily for 4 weeks, given with each rifampicin dose, grouped as in
Figures 4-6 into a 300-1200 mg/day and a 1650-2100 mg/day rifampicin category.
Only the category enters the model, so each subject's dose is drawn from the
doses in its category. There are 200 subjects per regimen x rifampicin
category.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
n_per_arm <- 200

arms <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  regimen = c("1200 mg QD", "600 mg BID"),
  rif_group = c("RIF 300-1200 mg", "RIF 1650-2100 mg")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = dplyr::row_number())

subjects <- arms |>
  dplyr::slice(rep(seq_len(dplyr::n()), each = n_per_arm)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    DOSE_RIFAMPICIN_MG = ifelse(
      rif_group == "RIF 300-1200 mg",
      sample(c(300, 450, 600, 1200), dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE),
      sample(c(1650, 2100), dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE)
    )
  )
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(subjects$id))

t_end <- 28 * 24
obs_times <- seq(0, t_end, by = 0.5)

make_events <- function(subj) {
  dose_amt <- ifelse(subj$regimen == "1200 mg QD", 1200, 600)
  dose_ii <- ifelse(subj$regimen == "1200 mg QD", 24, 12)
  dose_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(subj)), function(i) {
    tt <- seq(0, t_end - dose_ii[i], by = dose_ii[i])
    data.frame(id = subj$id[i], time = tt, amt = dose_amt[i], evid = 1L,
               cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  }))
  obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = subj$id, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      subj |> dplyr::select(id, regimen, rif_group, DOSE_RIFAMPICIN_MG),
      by = "id"
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

events <- make_events(subjects)
```

The model declares two endpoints (plasma `Cc` and CSF `Ccsf`), so observation
rows name the ODE state `central` and carry `dvid = 1`; rxode2 then returns
both `Cc` and `Ccsf` at every observation time.

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Purohit_2026_linezolid")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = events,
  keep = c("regimen", "rif_group", "DOSE_RIFAMPICIN_MG"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, Ccsf, regimen, rif_group)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 4: concentration-time profiles over the first 72 hours

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 4 of Purohit 2026: median and 95% interval of simulated
# plasma (A, B) and CSF (C, D) linezolid concentrations.
fig4 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 72) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, Ccsf), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(matrix = ifelse(matrix == "Cc", "Plasma", "CSF")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(matrix, regimen, rif_group, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q025 = quantile(conc, 0.025), q50 = median(conc),
    q975 = quantile(conc, 0.975), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    matrix = factor(matrix, levels = c("Plasma", "CSF")),
    rif_group = factor(rif_group, levels = c("RIF 300-1200 mg", "RIF 1650-2100 mg"))
  )

ggplot(fig4, aes(time, q50, colour = regimen, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q025, ymax = q975), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_grid(matrix ~ rif_group, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 72, 12)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Linezolid concentration (mg/L)",
       colour = "Linezolid", fill = "Linezolid",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Purohit 2026. Dashed line: MIC 1 mg/L.")
```

## Figures 5 and 6: time above the MIC over 4 weeks

The paper reports the percentage of time that plasma (Figure 5) and CSF
(Figure 6) linezolid concentrations stay above an MIC of 1 mg/L over the
4-week simulated course. Here it is the fraction of the 0.5-hour grid points
above 1 mg/L, averaged over subjects.

```{r figure-5-6}
tmic <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time < t_end) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, rif_group, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    plasma = mean(Cc > 1) * 100,
    csf = mean(Ccsf > 1) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, rif_group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(plasma = mean(plasma), csf = mean(csf), .groups = "drop")

published_tmic <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,      ~rif_group,          ~plasma_pub, ~csf_pub,
  "1200 mg QD", "RIF 300-1200 mg",    86.2,        88.3,
  "600 mg BID", "RIF 300-1200 mg",    99.9,        99.7,
  "1200 mg QD", "RIF 1650-2100 mg",   70.4,        77.1,
  "600 mg BID", "RIF 1650-2100 mg",   99.5,        99.2
)

tmic_cmp <- dplyr::left_join(published_tmic, tmic, by = c("regimen", "rif_group")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    plasma_diff = plasma - plasma_pub,
    csf_diff = csf - csf_pub
  )

tmic_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, rif_group, plasma_pub, plasma, csf_pub, csf) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Linezolid" = regimen,
    "Rifampicin" = rif_group,
    "Plasma T>MIC, published (%)" = plasma_pub,
    "Plasma T>MIC, simulated (%)" = plasma,
    "CSF T>MIC, published (%)" = csf_pub,
    "CSF T>MIC, simulated (%)" = csf
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = paste(
    "Percentage of time above an MIC of 1 mg/L over 4 weeks.",
    "Published values: Figures 5 and 6 and Results of Purohit 2026."
  ))

tmic_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(source = "Simulated") |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, rif_group, source, Plasma = plasma, CSF = csf) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    published_tmic |>
      dplyr::mutate(source = "Published") |>
      dplyr::select(regimen, rif_group, source, Plasma = plasma_pub, CSF = csf_pub)
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Plasma, CSF), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "tmic") |>
  dplyr::mutate(matrix = factor(matrix, levels = c("Plasma", "CSF"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(rif_group, tmic, fill = regimen, alpha = source)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), colour = "black") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(Published = 0.45, Simulated = 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~matrix) +
  labs(x = "Rifampicin dose", y = "Time above MIC (%)", fill = "Linezolid",
       alpha = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figures 5 (plasma) and 6 (CSF) of Purohit 2026.")
```

The simulated percentages agree with the published values to within about
1.5 percentage points. The once-daily regimen is the sensitive one: a 34%
change in clearance moves its plasma T>MIC by about 16 points (86% to 70%), so
the gate below fails on a mis-transcribed clearance, volume, absorption rate
or covariate effect. The means are over 200 subjects per arm; across two
seeds the largest difference from the published value was 1.2 points (CSF,
once daily with high-dose rifampicin), so a 4-point tolerance leaves headroom
for a different cohort draw without being able to pass a wrong model.

```{r tmic-gate}
stopifnot(
  all(abs(tmic_cmp$plasma_diff) < 4),
  all(abs(tmic_cmp$csf_diff) < 4)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA is run separately for plasma and CSF over the first dosing day
(0-24 h) and a steady-state day (day 14, 312-336 h), grouped by regimen and
rifampicin category. The day-1 Cmin is the pre-dose zero at time 0; the
day-14 Cmin is the steady-state trough.

```{r pknca}
nca_window <- function(df) {
  df |> dplyr::filter(time <= 24 | (time >= 312 & time <= 336))
}

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  nca_window() |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste(regimen, rif_group, sep = " | ")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 312), end = c(24, 336),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cmin = TRUE
)

run_nca <- function(conc_col) {
  conc_df <- sim |>
    nca_window() |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste(regimen, rif_group, sep = " | ")) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, treatment, conc = dplyr::all_of(conc_col)) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc))
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}

nca_plasma <- run_nca("Cc")
nca_csf <- run_nca("Ccsf")

summarise_nca <- function(res) {
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "cmin")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(day = ifelse(start == 0, "Day 1", "Day 14")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(treatment, day, PPTESTCD) |>
    dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
}

summarise_nca(nca_plasma) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen | rifampicin" = treatment, "Day" = day,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)" = auclast, "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Plasma linezolid NCA (simulated medians).")

summarise_nca(nca_csf) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen | rifampicin" = treatment, "Day" = day,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)" = auclast, "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "CSF linezolid NCA (simulated medians).")
```

## Comparison against published values

The paper reports no NCA table. The reference values below are the peak
median concentrations over the first 24 hours, digitised by the maintainers
from Figure 4 (about +/- 0.5 mg/L reading precision for plasma and +/- 0.3
mg/L for CSF; for the twice-daily regimen the second-dose peak is the
higher one).

```{r nca-compare}
fig4_ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                             ~matrix,  ~cmax,
  "1200 mg QD | RIF 300-1200 mg",         "Plasma", 21.0,
  "600 mg BID | RIF 300-1200 mg",         "Plasma", 12.2,
  "1200 mg QD | RIF 1650-2100 mg",        "Plasma", 18.5,
  "600 mg BID | RIF 1650-2100 mg",        "Plasma", 10.0,
  "1200 mg QD | RIF 300-1200 mg",         "CSF",    8.6,
  "600 mg BID | RIF 300-1200 mg",         "CSF",    5.3,
  "1200 mg QD | RIF 1650-2100 mg",        "CSF",    7.2,
  "600 mg BID | RIF 1650-2100 mg",        "CSF",    4.3
)

day1 <- function(res) {
  as.data.frame(res) |> dplyr::filter(start == 0)
}

cmp <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    simulated = day1(nca_plasma) |> dplyr::mutate(matrix = "Plasma"),
    reference = fig4_ref |> dplyr::filter(matrix == "Plasma"),
    by = c("treatment", "matrix"), params = "cmax",
    units = c(cmax = "mg/L"), tolerance_pct = 20
  ),
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    simulated = day1(nca_csf) |> dplyr::mutate(matrix = "CSF"),
    reference = fig4_ref |> dplyr::filter(matrix == "CSF"),
    by = c("treatment", "matrix"), params = "cmax",
    units = c(cmax = "mg/L"), tolerance_pct = 20
  )
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Simulated day-1 Cmax (median) vs. the Figure 4 median peak.",
  "* differs from reference by >20%."
))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Table 2 vs. Results text.** The Results text quotes the partition
  coefficient as 53.8% and kp as 0.382 1/h, whereas Table 2 gives 0.535 and
  0.383 1/h. The model uses the Table 2 final estimates; the differences are
  below 1%.
- **IIV scale.** Table 2 states that interindividual variability is
  expressed as a percent coefficient of variation, so the variances are
  `log(1 + CV^2)`. The table gives no confidence interval for the IIV rows,
  so the scale cannot be checked numerically. Reading the percentages as
  `sqrt(omega^2)` instead changes the simulated T>MIC by less than 0.5
  points, so the Figure 5 and 6 comparison does not separate the two
  readings either.
- **Rifampicin dose effect.** The paper treats the daily rifampicin dose as
  categorical and reports a single effect for 1650 or 2100 mg relative to
  300-1200 mg. The model encodes it as `DOSE_RIFAMPICIN_MG >= 1650`. The
  weight-band doses of 750 mg (standard arm, >= 71 kg) and 2550 mg (high-dose
  arm, >= 71 kg) were not observed; the threshold places them in the
  reference and high categories, which is an extrapolation.
- **CSF compartment.** The paper describes CSF concentrations "as levels
  within a hypothetical effect compartment" with a rate (kp) and an extent
  (PC) of entry. It is implemented as `d/dt(csf) = kp * (PC * Cc - csf)`,
  with `csf` holding a concentration and no mass removed from plasma. The
  paper's `kp` is named `ke0` and `PC` is named `ppc`, following the
  library's effect-compartment conventions.
- **Residual error.** The plasma combined additive and proportional error is
  encoded with nlmixr2's `add() + prop()`. The paper does not say whether its
  NONMEM error model summed the variances or the standard deviations.
- **Simulation design.** The paper's simulations drew demographics from the
  18 trial participants over 500 trials. No covariate other than the
  rifampicin dose category enters the model, so 200 subjects per regimen and
  rifampicin category are simulated here, with doses drawn from the doses in
  each category.
- **Figure 4 reference values** were digitised by the maintainers and are
  approximate.
- No erratum or correction notice was found on Europe PMC as of 2026-11-12.
